title: service-tag-driven-rbac-region-pin-gatekeeper
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a service-tag driven RBAC v2 translator and a region-pinning gateway that enforces tenant residency constraints and routes KMS key usage to region-appropriate backends. Includes audit header enrichment and a canary rollout plan.
body:
Motivation: Customers require fine-grained service-level RBAC that can be mapped from onboarding metadata (service tags) into RBAC v2 bindings, and a non-intrusive enforcement layer that enforces data residency/region pinning for KMS usage while keeping audit trails intact. This PR introduces a 'Gatekeeper' proxy and an RBAC transformer pipeline that together provide: 1) deterministic translation of service tags -> RBAC v2 subject/role bindings, 2) region-pin enforcement at the service ingress with safe fallbacks, 3) a KMS routing shim that selects the tenant-backed CMK provider based on residency rules, and 4) audit header enrichment and signed provenance for downstream long-term storage.

High level changes: - new service-tag-to-rbac transformer (service/integration/transformer) that consumes onboarding claims and emits RBAC v2 delta patches; supports multiple mapping profiles and an allowlist mode for gradual rollout. - gatekeeper proxy (service/gatekeeper) that intercepts internal API calls, validates region assertions, enforces tenancy pinning, resolves KMS target using a configurable resolver, and injects canonical audit headers (x-rw-audit-provenance, x-rw-region-assertion). - kms-routing shim (service/kms-resolver) that implements affinity scoring for preferred KMS providers and falls back to multi-provider wrap/unwrap when strict residency is not met. - migration tooling and a linear task to backfill existing services with tags (scripts/migrations/backfill-service-tags). - unit + integration tests and a simple canary rollout orchestration script for Redwood Dedicated.

Design notes: The transformer uses a small declarative mapping language (YAML profiles) so security owners can express tag -> role mappings without code changes. RBAC patches are additive and annotated; we also emit a migration report to detect potential privilege escalations. The gatekeeper enforces region pinning using an assertion matcher that supports regex patterns and explicit lists; enforcement modes: monitor (log-only), audit-fail (deny and emit structured audit), strict (deny and require manual approval). KMS routing honors the tenant residency policy; if a strict residency mismatch occurs and strict mode is enabled, the request returns a 403 with a structured audit entry and an operator alert.

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests: transformer mapping edge cases, rule conflicts, malformed tags. - Integration tests: gatekeeper end-to-end with KMS shim using local test harness and a fake KMS provider. - Canary strategy: deploy Gatekeeper in monitor mode for 48h on 5% of traffic, then audit-fail for 24h with operator notification, then strict for canary subset before global switch.

Checklist (all completed): - [x] Mapping language schema and validation. - [x] Gatekeeper request/response contract and SDK shim. - [x] KMS resolver with provider selection heuristics. - [x] Audit header enrichment and cryptographic provenance signer. - [x] Migration script and backfill dry-run. - [x] Unit and integration tests. - [x] Docs: security runbook and operator playbook.

Commits summary: - commit 1: add transformer skeleton and mapping schema (service/integration/transformer/*). - commit 2: implement gatekeeper proxy and request interceptor (service/gatekeeper/*). - commit 3: add kms resolver and provider adapters (service/kms-resolver/*). - commit 4: audit enrichment, signing helper, and tests. - commit 5: migration backfill and canary script + docs.

Files touched (high level): ["service/gatekeeper/gatekeeper.go", "service/gatekeeper/routes.go", "service/integration/transformer/mapping.go", "service/integration/transformer/schema.yml", "service/kms-resolver/resolver.go", "scripts/migrations/backfill-service-tags.py", "docs/security/gatekeeper-runbook.md", "tests/integration/gatekeeper_kms_test.go", "pkg/audit/provenance_signer.go", "deploy/canary/gatekeeper-canary.yaml", "configs/rbac/mapping-profiles/default.yml", "helm/charts/gatekeeper/values.yaml"].

Review conversation summary: - Arjun Patel: "Can we make the transformer mapping strict by default? I worry about silent privilege expansion." Response (Maya): "Default is conservative: mappings are additive and validation rejects mappings that introduce 'admin' role unless explicitly allowed via profile flag. Added tests to verify." - Lena Vogel: "How does this interact with existing operator-scoped RBAC delegations?" Response (Maya): "Gatekeeper respects operator delegations; transformer emits annotations and we consult existing delegation graph during delta calculation. Added a delegated_check in the resolver." - Tomás Alvarez (security): "Audit provenance signer needs key rotation support and proof-of-possession for auditors." Response (Maya): "Implemented signer interface with KMS-backed key wrapping and rotation metadata; included rotation test harness. Added docs for auditors on signature verification."

CI summary: - build: pass - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests (gated): pass in final run after rebase - lint: pass - security-scan (SAST): one low-severity finding fixed in commit 4

Merge & post-merge: Merged via squash on 2025-10-14 after approvals from Arjun and Lena and security signoff from Tomás. Post-merge tasks scheduled: - enable monitor mode for 5% traffic (ops/infra ticket) - run backfill dry-run on non-prod and submit migration report - add RBAC mapping profiles for top 20 tenants (migration ticket linked)

Rollout risks and mitigations: - Risk: transformer mis-mapping could grant broader roles. Mitigation: mappings require explicit allow flags and we run a preflight comparator against a snapshot of current bindings. - Risk: KMS fallback could expose data transit outside region. Mitigation: strict mode exists and operator alerting created; fallback requires explicit opt-in for tenants. - Risk: increased latency for calls proxied through Gatekeeper. Mitigation: added lightweight cache for region assertions and async audit flush to avoid p99 regressions.

Related: ENG-7621 (mapping framework), SEC-193 (audit provenance), SUP-4712 (customer support case that motivated strict mode). Contact: Maya Chen @maya for follow-ups and rollout coordination.
